title: Philanthropy: Humankind and Loving It
summary: Josh and Chuck explore philanthropy, starting with the everyday meaning of giving money or time without expecting anything in return. They discuss the Gates Foundation's giving pledge, Warren Buffett, Steve Jobs's lack of recorded charitable giving, historical foundations like Rockefeller, Carnegie and Ford, and giving statistics (who gives, how much, to which causes). The hosts cover how to vet a charity (program vs. overhead spending, guidestar and other watchdogs, state registration), charity scams, direct mail and list selling, ways to donate (cash, checks, online, bequests, goods, cars), and US tax code categories (501(c)(3), private foundations, 501(c)(4), 501(c)(6)) and deductions. They also touch on volunteering's estimated value, tithing, and the possible expiration of Bush-era tax cuts. The episode ends with a listener-mail style plug for Cooperative for Education (CoEd) in Guatemala and Thanksgiving wishes.

segments.title: Opening banter and Science Channel plug
segments.summary: Josh asks listeners to support his mustache fundraiser for prostate cancer research, then plugs Science Channel's Punkin Chunking broadcast. Chuck and Josh welcome producer Jerry back and introduce the idea that philanthropy means giving without getting something in return.

segments.title: What philanthropy is and donating time
segments.summary: The hosts define philanthropy as giving money or time without a sale, noting it means love of humankind. They discuss volunteering time versus money, and tax deductions for volunteer travel costs.

segments.title: Billionaire giving: Gates pledge, Buffett, Steve Jobs
segments.summary: They discuss the Gates Foundation's giving pledge, Warren Buffett's bequest to the foundation, and the lack of any recorded charitable giving by Steve Jobs. Ted Turner's billion-dollar donation to the UN is mentioned.

segments.title: Historical foundations and who gives
segments.summary: The hosts compare modern billionaire giving to early 20th-century foundations by the Rockefellers and Carnegies, and note that the poorest Americans give the highest share of income.

segments.title: Charitable giving statistics
segments.summary: Figures are discussed: the number of US charities, total charitable giving in 2011 (about $298 billion), the share from individuals, and giving by source such as foundations, bequests and corporations. Corporate giving through grocery store charity drives is questioned.

segments.title: Vetting charities and overhead costs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how a charity should spend money, with about 75 percent or more going to programs, the reasons fundraising costs vary, and resources for checking charities such as Guidestar, the Better Business Bureau, the Foundation Center and state charity offices.

segments.title: Charity scams and direct mail tactics
segments.summary: A Texas man who set up a fake post-tornado charity that collected checks and kept the money is discussed. Josh describes how charities sell and swap donor mailing lists and how to opt out of solicitations.

segments.title: Ways to donate: cash, checks, online, bequests, goods
segments.summary: The hosts describe how to give cash, checks and online donations with records, bequests in wills, and donating goods such as cars, computers and office or emergency supplies, along with the write-off rules for goods and auction purchases.

segments.title: US tax code categories for charities
segments.summary: The hosts explain IRS categories: 501(c)(3) public charities, private foundations, and private operating foundations, with deduction limits. They also cover 501(c)(4) social welfare groups, 501(c)(6) trade associations, and which contributions are deductible.

segments.title: Volunteering value, tithing and tax cuts
segments.summary: The hosts cite an estimated value of volunteer time, discuss volunteer frustrations, and note that tithing may be deductible. Mitt Romney's donations and Bill Maher's criticism are mentioned, church budget breakdowns are shared, and the possible expiration of Bush tax cuts and their effect on deductions is raised.

segments.title: Cooperative for Education (CoEd) plug and Thanksgiving sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck promote Cooperative for Education in Guatemala, which funds textbooks and computer labs through a self-sustaining rental model, and offer Thanksgiving wishes and contact information.
